dimensions.assessment: Affects hourly employees and employers nationwide who offer voluntary education or training programs outside regular working hours.
dimensions.evidence: any time spent attending or participating in an education or training program or a similar activity

dimensions.assessment: Changes compensation requirements by ensuring voluntary off-hours training does not count toward compensable hours or overtime.
dimensions.evidence: there shall be excluded... any time spent attending or participating in an education or training program

dimensions.assessment: Could reduce overtime labor costs for employers and corresponding wage earnings for employees participating in voluntary training, though specific economic totals are absent.
Amends Section 3(o) of the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 regarding the definition of hours worked.
dimensions.evidence: To amend the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 to exclude certain activities from hours worked

dimensions.assessment: Applies permanently to hours worked on or after the date of enactment.
dimensions.evidence: The amendment made by subsection (a) shall apply with respect to hours worked on or after the date of enactment of this Act.

missing_information: The number of workers or employers impacted by this change is not quantified.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill amends the Fair Labor Standards Act to exclude voluntary, out-of-hours employee training and education programs from the definition of hours worked, affecting overtime and wage calculations.

related.title: Providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 2988) to amend the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 to specify requirements concerning the consideration of pecuniary and non-pecuniary factors, and for other purposes; providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 2262) to amend the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 to exclude certain activities from hours worked, and for other purposes; providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 2270) to amend the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 to exclude child and dependent care services and payments from the rate used to compute overtime compensation; providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 2312) to amend the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 to revise the definition of the term ''tipped employee'', and for other purposes; and providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 4366) to clarify the treatment of 2 or more employers as joint employers under the National Labor Relations Act and the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938.
